interpretive_limits: The book calls 2^-52 machine epsilon for binary64 and derives a nearest-rounding bound of half that amount; the library convention names unit roundoff u=2^-53. Do not interchange the two constants.
The book is a teaching text: several general proofs are deferred to advanced linear algebra sources, and its Householder QR section does not prove the finite-precision backward-stability bound.
The normal-equations section proves the exact least-squares characterization and condition-number squaring; it does not prove a computed QR least-squares solution backward-stable.

interpretive_limits: Goldberg distinguishes ulps from relative error, analyzes exact rounding and IEEE exceptions, and discusses stability examples; it does not establish the library’s current dot-product, GEPP, Cholesky, or Householder QR theorem contracts.
The ACM paper uses its own machine-epsilon/base/precision notation. The library’s standard relative model and unit-roundoff convention govern any local theorem.
